title: Set Up the Modern JavaScript Lab
content:
# Set Up the Modern JavaScript Lab

This section studies JavaScript features that TypeScript understands and can compile for different runtimes. Keep authored TypeScript in `src`, generated JavaScript in `dist`, and let one project configuration control the build.

## Project shape

```text
next-gen-lab/
├─ src/
│  └─ app.ts
├─ dist/
│  └─ app.js
├─ index.html
├─ package.json
└─ tsconfig.json
```

Install TypeScript and a lightweight development server, then start the compiler in watch mode beside the server.

```bash
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev typescript lite-server
npx tsc --init
npx tsc --watch
npx lite-server
```

The browser needs the DOM declarations; the compiler target determines how modern syntax is emitted. Source maps keep browser debugging connected to `src/app.ts`.

## Complete subclass code — `tsconfig.json`

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES6",
    "lib": ["DOM", "ES6", "DOM.Iterable", "ScriptHost"],
    "rootDir": "./src",
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "sourceMap": true,
    "strict": true
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

## Complete subclass code — `package.json`

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc",
    "dev:types": "tsc --watch",
    "dev:web": "lite-server"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "lite-server": "^2.6.1",
    "typescript": "^5.9.0"
  }
}
```

questions.question: Why separate src and dist?
options: To keep authored TypeScript apart from emitted JavaScript
questions.explanation: The source/output boundary prevents generated files from becoming authored inputs.

questions.question: What does target control?
options: The JavaScript syntax emitted by TypeScript
questions.explanation: Target selects the JavaScript language level of compiler output.

title: Use `let`, `const` & Block Scope

questions.question: Which declaration best fits a binding that is never reassigned?
questions.explanation: Const communicates and enforces that the binding stays fixed.

questions.question: Where is a let declared inside an if block available?
options: Only inside that block and its nested blocks

title: Write Arrow Functions & Typed Callbacks

questions.question: When may an arrow function omit return?
options: When its body is a single returned expression
questions.explanation: An expression body returns that expression implicitly.

questions.question: Why can TypeScript infer the click event parameter?
options: The event-listener signature provides contextual typing
questions.explanation: The API overload and event name give the callback a known parameter type.

title: Apply Default Function Parameters

questions.question: Where should a defaulted parameter usually appear?
questions.explanation: Trailing defaults let callers omit arguments naturally.

questions.question: What does add(5) return when b defaults to 1?
questions.explanation: The omitted second argument uses its default value.

title: Copy & Combine with the Spread Operator

questions.question: What does activeHobbies.push(...hobbies) do?
options: Passes each hobby as a separate push argument
questions.explanation: Spread expands the source array into individual arguments.

questions.question: Is { ...person } a deep copy of every nested value?
options: No, spread creates a shallow copy
questions.explanation: Nested references remain shared unless they are copied explicitly.

title: Collect Values with Rest Parameters

questions.question: What does a rest parameter create inside the function?
questions.explanation: Rest merges the remaining call arguments into an array.

questions.question: When is a tuple rest type useful?
options: When the function requires an exact number and order of arguments
questions.explanation: A tuple captures fixed arity and positional types.

title: Destructure Arrays & Objects

questions.question: How does array destructuring choose values?
questions.explanation: Array patterns map variables to ordered elements.

questions.question: What does firstName: userName mean in object destructuring?
options: Extract firstName into a local named userName
questions.explanation: The colon introduces a local alias in an object binding pattern.

title: Compile Modern Syntax for Older Runtimes

questions.question: What happens to modern JavaScript syntax when target changes to ES5?
options: TypeScript rewrites unsupported syntax into older equivalents
questions.explanation: Target controls the language level of generated JavaScript.

questions.question: Does TypeScript automatically polyfill every modern runtime API?
questions.explanation: Compilation can transform syntax, but missing runtime APIs need separate polyfills or a newer runtime.
